question: Of 1,000 twin pairs, 340 are boy–girl. Fraternal pairs come out mixed-sex about half the time. How many pairs are identical?
move: Use the cases you can identify to count the ones that look alike.
trap: Counting all 660 same-sex pairs as identical, as if fraternal twins were always mixed.
hint: Mixed-sex pairs can only be fraternal; ask how many fraternal pairs hide among the same-sex ones.
steps: Fraternal pairs split evenly between mixed-sex and same-sex.
So same-sex fraternal pairs also number about 340.

diagram.label: twin pairs
diagram.caption: Of 660 same-sex pairs, 340 are fraternal, as many as the mixed pairs; only 320 are identical.

reference: Fellman and Eriksson, Weinberg's differential rule reconsidered, Human Biology, 2006
